title: Lenny Kravitz Gets Into His Future Son-In-Law Harry Styles’ ‘Adore You’ at MSG
summary: The rock icon was on his feet for the show with his daughter Zoë Kravitz at the pop star's New York residency.
contentText:
Lenny Kravitz may be one of rock’s most recognizable faces, but at a Harry Styles show, you might find him looking less like a musical legend and more like a very enthusiastic future father-in-law.

Kravitz was recently spotted dancing along from the crowd as Styles performed “Sign of the Times” during his Wednesday night (Sept. 23) concert at the famous New York venue, Madison Square Garden. His daughter, Zoë Kravitz — who is engaged to Styles — was standing beside him, joining her dad for the show.

The sweetest moment, though, was when Styles spotted the father-daughter duo during “Adore You.”

As he sang the 2019 hit, Styles noticed Kravitz and Zoë in the audience and flashed them a peace sign from the stage. Zoë seemed to return the gesture with a small smile, while her dad continued to sway to the music.

The song in which Styles acknowledged the duo is somewhat fitting, considering the song’s theme. The track was released as the third single from his 2019 album Fine Line , and the song easily became one of his biggest solo hits. It reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 50 weeks on the chart.

Kravitz wasn’t exactly watching a pop star in the making. He was watching Styles’ most recent album, Kiss All the Time. Disco, Occasionally come to life after a successful time on the Billboard 200 , peaking at No. 1 upon its release. Styles is currently on his Together, Together New York City residency, blending old hits like “Adore You” with his new disco-influenced songs.

Styles has plenty of history with the Kravitz family offstage as well. He and Zoë confirmed their engagement in April after being first romantically linked in 2025. Lenny has previously spoken positively about meeting Styles, and his appearance at Wednesday’s show gave fans a glimpse into how intertwined the family really is.
